name: vwap_slope_trend_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: The slope of VWAP over a rolling 20-bar window reveals the direction of institutional net order flow. A rising VWAP slope means institutions are net buying at progressively higher prices; a falling slope means net selling. Trading in the direction of the VWAP slope captures the institutional order flow tailwind. The edge exists because most participants look at price vs VWAP (static level), not the rate of change of VWAP (dynamic signal). The slope change anticipates future VWAP-tracking algo behavior — if VWAP is rising, TWAP/VWAP algos will bid higher. This edge persists because computing and interpreting VWAP slope is non-trivial and requires clean real-time data.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND close > 50 INR

long.confirmation: vwap_slope has been positive for 5+ consecutive bars AND increasing for last 3 bars

short.confirmation: vwap_slope has been negative for 5+ consecutive bars AND decreasing for last 3 bars

entry.entry_price: limit order at EMA(close, 9) if within 0.1% of current price, else market

exit.target: 0.5% from entry OR vwap_slope reverses sign
exit.signal_exit: exit if vwap_slope crosses zero (trend exhaustion)

filters.vix_filter: no specific filter — trend strategies work across VIX regimes
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:45 (slope needs data) or after 15:00
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 slope should align (both positive or both negative for added confidence)
filters.event_filter: caution on RBI policy day — slope can reverse suddenly on rate decision

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — slope analysis is straightforward once implemented but not widely used on VWAP

weaknesses: VWAP slope is a lagging indicator — by the time slope confirms a trend, much of the move may be done
In choppy markets with ADX < 20, slope oscillates around zero giving false signals; ADX filter helps but reduces opportunity set
Slope calculation via linear regression is sensitive to outlier bars — a single large bar can distort slope reading
prior_art: VWAP slope analysis is discussed in Brian Shannon's 'Technical Analysis Using Multiple Timeframes'. Linear regression slope on price is a standard indicator (LinReg Slope in most platforms). Applying it to VWAP specifically rather than price is less common in literature. ADX as trend filter is from Wilder (1978).
notes: Edge math: 0.50 * 50bps - 0.50 * 30bps = 25 - 15 = 10 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps RT. Net ≈ -1 bps. Marginally negative on conservative estimates. However, the trailing stop should improve avg winner beyond 50 bps in trending conditions. If avg winner is 60 bps: 0.50*60 - 0.50*30 = 15 bps gross, net 4 bps. Needs validation.
